prose.label: MCAS.
prose.text: {{web-who-users}} The MCAS feed's Who group lists Locations where those articles list Users, which does not settle whether MCAS filters by user {{gap:mcas-who-group}}.

web-who-users.statement: The TCP, HTTP and Cloud web feed articles each list a Users filter under Who, which limits the logs to specific users who generated transactions.

quotes: Users: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific users who generated transactions.
Users: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific users who generated transactions.
Users: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific users who generated transactions.

filters-and.statement: The TCP web feed article says admins can configure multiple filter types and gives one example: if an admin selects the location HQ and the department Finance, the NSS selects logs that belong to both the HQ location and Finance department. It adds that a large number of filters or complex filters, such as string searches, can impact NSS performance.

quotes: For example, if an admin selects the location HQ and the department Finance, the NSS selects logs that belong to both the HQ location and Finance department.
A large number of filters or complex filters, such as string searches, can impact the NSS performance.

wildcards.statement: The web feed's Referer URLs filter accepts wildcards; the quoted rule is that *string is suffix matching, matching URLs ending with 'string'. Multiple strings are allowed, one per line, and string search is not case-sensitive.

quotes: *string -> Suffix matching match URLs ending with ‘string’
evidence.after: Referer URLs: Use this filter to limit the logs based on the Referer URL in the HTTP header. You can use wildcards based on the rules:

quotes: Multiple strings are allowed. Enter one string per line, then click Add Items. String search is not case-sensitive.

include-exclude-defaults.statement: The URL Classes filter has an Include option, enabled by default with the default value Any, and an Exclude option whose default value is None.

quotes: Include: Use this filter to include selected URL classes in the logs. This filter is enabled by default. The default value for this filter is Any.
Exclude: Use this filter to exclude selected URL classes from the logs. The default value for this filter is None.

category-threat-coupling.statement: The URL Categories filter falls under the same filter class as the Advanced Threats filter: if at least one advanced threat is selected, the specific URL categories to include must also be selected, and when at least one URL category is selected, the default Any option in the Advanced Threats filter does not apply.

quotes: The URL Categories filter falls under the same filter class as the Advanced Threats filter. This means if you select at least one advanced threat, then you must also select the specific URL categories that you want included in the logs.
When you select at least one URL category, the default Any option in the Advanced Threats filter does not apply.

users-select-all.statement: In the web feed's Users filter, Select All selects all results, deleted users appear with a strikethrough line, and Hide Deleted hides them from the list.

quotes: Click Select All to select all results. Deleted users appear with a strikethrough line. Select Hide Deleted to hide these deleted users from the list.

ip-entry-forms.statement: The Client IP Addresses filter accepts a range of IP addresses (for example 192.0.2.1-192.0.2.10), and for item lists up to 500 items can be viewed on a page.

quotes: A range of IP addresses (e.g., 192.0.2.1-192.0.2.10)
For item lists, you can view up to 500 items on a page
evidence.after: Client IP Addresses: Use this filter to limit the logs based on a client’s private IP address. You can enter:

web-policy-action.statement: In the web feed's policy action filter, transactions for which the service displayed a Caution page are considered blocked, and if users proceed they are considered allowed. Policy Reason values are the policy reason strings that are in transaction drilldown.

quotes: Transactions wherein the service displayed a Caution page are considered blocked transactions; if users proceed with the transactions, they are considered allowed.
These are the policy reason strings that are in transaction drilldown.

public-ip-meaning.statement: The internal IP address is available if traffic is forwarded to the service through a GRE or VPN tunnel or from the XFF header; if the internal IP address is not available, the value is the same as the client IP address.

quotes: The internal IP address is available if traffic forwarding is forwarded to the service through a GRE or VPN tunnel or from the XFF header. If the internal IP address is not available, the value is the same as the client IP address.

web-transaction-filters.statement: The web feed's supported protocols are HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP. Request size filters use bytes by default, and KB, MB, GB or TB can be specified, for example 10KB-1MB or 200.

quotes: Supported protocols are HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP.
By default, the service uses bytes, but you can also specify KB, MB, GB, or TB (e.g., 10KB-1MB, 200).
evidence.after: Request Sizes: Use this filter to limit the logs based on HTTP request size.

web-security-filters.statement: The Suspicious Content filter limits logs by the Page Risk Index score of a transaction, a single value or a range between 0 and 100. Encrypted File in the unscannable options means encrypted or password-protected files, and the Miscellaneous <Cloud Application Category> Apps option represents all the newly added lesser-known predefined applications for a category.

quotes: Suspicious Content: Use this filter to limit the logs based on the Page Risk Index score of a transaction. Enter either a single value or a range of values, between 0 and 100.
Encrypted File: Encrypted or password-protected (e.g., GZIP, PDF)
The Miscellaneous <Cloud Application Category> Apps (e.g., Miscellaneous Finance Apps) option in this filter represents all the newly added lesser-known predefined applications

cloud-aiml-http-url-classes.statement: The Cloud NSS web feed has an AI/ML Detection Source filter that limits logs by the AI/ML detection source for the transaction, and the HTTP web feed article's URL Classes filter says to select the classes to include, with multiple selections allowed.

quotes: AI/ML Detection Source: Use this filter to limit the logs based on the AI/ML detection source for the transaction.
URL Classes: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific URL classes. Select those that you want to include. Multiple selections are allowed.

firewall-actions.statement: Firewall feed filters include Block/ICMP, packets dropped because they matched a Firewall rule and sent the client an ICMP error of Type 3 and code 9 or 10; Block/Reset, which for TCP traffic drops the matching packets and sends the client a TCP reset and for non-TCP traffic is the same as Block/Drop; IPS Reset, packets reset due to IPS policy; the DNAT Policy Action, for traffic on which the service performed destination NAT; and Client Destination Names, a destination FQDN filter for Advanced Firewall.

quotes: Block/ICMP: Packets that were dropped because they matched a Firewall rule and sent the client an ICMP error message of Type 3 (Destination Unreachable) and code 9 or 10 (network/host administratively prohibited).
Block/Reset: For TCP traffic, the Zscaler service drops all packets that match the Firewall rule and sends the client a TCP reset.
For non-TCP traffic, it's the same as Block/Drop.
IPS Reset: Packets that were reset due to IPS policy.
DNAT Policy Action: Use this filter to limit the logs to traffic on which the service performed destination NAT and redirected traffic to specific IP addresses and optionally, ports.
Client Destination Names: For Advanced Firewall, use this filter to limit the logs to traffic associated with a specific destination FQDN.

firewall-aggregate-addresses.statement: For aggregated sessions, the client destination IP address filter value is that of the last session in the aggregate, and the Countries filter is the country code that corresponds to the server IP address.

quotes: For aggregated sessions, this is the client destination IP address of the last session in the aggregate.
Countries: The country code that corresponds to the server IP address.

dns-actions.statement: DNS feed filters include Redirect, limiting logs to transactions in which the service redirected the DNS request or response, and Response Redirect, limiting logs to DNS responses the service redirected. Rule Names filter on specific rules in the DNS Control policy. The DNS Responses filter limits logs to sessions that contained specific data in the DNS responses, and domain names, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses can be specified there.

quotes: Redirect: Use this filter to limit the logs to transactions wherein the service redirected the DNS request or response.
Response Redirect: Use this filter to limit the logs to DNS responses that the service redirected.
Rule Names: Use this filter to limit the logs based on specific rules in the DNS Control policy.
DNS Responses: Use this filter to limit the logs to sessions that contained specific data in the DNS responses. You can specify domain names, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

tunnel-records.statement: A tunnel feed can send multiple tunnel log record types in a single feed: IKE Phase 1 (details for IPSec Phase 1 negotiation, IPSec only), Sample (statistics collected in 60-second sample windows, GRE and IPSec) and Tunnel Event (status change events, GRE and IPSec).

quotes: You can select multiple tunnel log record types (e.g., IKE Phase 2, Sample) to send in a single NSS feed.
IKE Phase 1: Details for IPSec Phase 1 negotiation (applies to IPSec only).
Sample: Statistics collected in 60-second sample windows (applies to both GRE and IPSec).
Tunnel Event: Status change events (applies to both GRE and IPSec).

tunnel-types.statement: The tunnel feed's Tunnel Type values include EAS Client Tunnel, the tunnel type for the extranet broker connection, and Z-Tunnel 2.0, which uses DTLS, TLS, or UDP, of which only Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector supports UDP. There is no limit to the number of VPN credentials that can be selected.

quotes: EAS Client Tunnel: The tunnel type for the extranet broker connection.
Z-Tunnel 2.0: Tunnel that uses DTLS, TLS, or UDP to send packets to the Zscaler service. Note that only Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector supports UDP.
There is no limit to the number of VPN credentials that you can select.

saas-app-categories.statement: A SaaS Security feed's Application Category limits the data to a specific category. The listed applications include Microsoft Dynamics 365, Citrix ShareFile, Smartsheet, ChatGPT, Jira Software and Bitbucket.

quotes: Application Category: Choose an application category to limit the data to a specific category:
Microsoft Dynamics 365
Citrix ShareFile
Smartsheet
- ChatGPT
Jira Software
Bitbucket

saas-policy-type-default.statement: By default the SaaS Security DLP and Malware policy types are not selected, so all incidents and violations, with or without a rule name, are exported through the NSS; DLP and Malware must be explicitly selected to export only incidents with valid rule names.

quotes: By default, the DLP and Malware policy types are not selected. Therefore, all incidents and violations with or without a rule name are exported through the NSS.
You must explicitly select DLP and Malware policy types from the list to export only the incidents with valid rule names through the NSS.

saas-event.statement: In the SaaS Security feed, Incident means a violation was detected in the scan and a configured DLP or malware rule was also triggered, and Violation means a violation was detected in the scan, either a DLP engine was matched or malware was detected. A feed configured with the earlier version of the filter remains supported until it is edited.

quotes: Incident: A violation was detected in the scan and a configured DLP or malware rule was also triggered.
Violation: A violation was detected in the scan (i.e., either a DLP engine was matched or malware was detected.)
Any NSS feed that you previously configured using the earlier version of the filter remains supported until you make any edits or changes to the feed.

saas-time-units.statement: The SaaS Security Scan Time filter, the time the Data at Rest Scanning policy took to scan content within the tenant, takes a specific value or a range with a dash; the default unit is milliseconds and MS or SEC can be specified, for example 10MS-100MS.

quotes: Scan Time: Filter logs based on the time the Data at Rest Scanning policy took to scan content within the tenant. Enter either a specific value or a range with a dash. The default unit of measure is milliseconds, but you can specify this unit using either MS or SEC (e.g., 10MS-100MS).

saas-unlimited-users.statement: The SaaS Security feed article says there is no limit to the number of users or departments that can be selected.

quotes: There's no limit to the number of users that you can select.
There's no limit to the number of departments that you can select.

saas-activity.statement: A SaaS Security Activity feed tracks activities, such as Create, Delete and Share, that users performed in the organization's sanctioned SaaS applications. If applicable the activity can have a second object listed, and the default option is None.

quotes: you can track activities (e.g., Create, Delete, Share) that users performed in your organization’s sanctioned SaaS applications.
If applicable, the activity can have a second object listed. The default option is None.

endpoint-dlp-record-type.statement: The Endpoint DLP Record Type filter distinguishes DLP incidents, user activities in which DLP policy rules were violated, from sensitive activities, in which movement of sensitive data was detected based on the file content.

quotes: DLP incidents are user activities in which DLP policy rules were violated. Sensitive activities are activities in which movement of sensitive data was detected based on the file content.

email-dlp-filters.statement: The Email DLP Record Type includes Scan, meaning the scan is normal with no DLP rule violation or movement of sensitive data detected. The Policy Action option Custom Header Insertion limits logs to transactions that resulted in a different action, such as quarantine, taken by the email application as defined by a custom header such as X-Zscaler-Scan:Quarantine, and the Severity filter limits logs to transactions associated with a specific DLP rule severity as configured in the Outbound Email Policy.

quotes: Scan: The scan is normal (i.e., no DLP rule violation or movement of sensitive data was detected.)

Select Custom Header Insertion to limit the logs to transactions that resulted in a different action (e.g., quarantine) taken by the email application (e.g., Microsoft Exchange) as defined by a custom header (e.g., X-Zscaler-Scan:Quarantine).
Severity: Use this filter to limit the logs to transactions associated with a specific DLP rule severity as configured in the Outbound Email Policy.

sandbox-filters.statement: The Sandbox Verdict Download File Type filter includes file types that are not eligible for Sandbox analysis, for which no log data is available. SHA limits logs by the SHA-256 hash of a file, and the verdicts filter covers Sandbox, Advanced Threat Protection and Malware Protection verdicts, optionally Benign for non-malicious verdicts. If no techniques are specified, verdicts associated with any possible MITRE ATT&CK technique are displayed.

quotes: This filter currently includes file types that are not eligible for Sandbox analysis. No log data is available for these file types, if selected.
SHA: Use this filter to limit the logs based on the SHA-256 hash of a file.

This filter includes verdicts related to Sandbox (e.g., Sandbox Adware), Advanced Threat Protection (e.g., Suspicious Content), and Malware Protection (e.g., Trojan) policies. Optionally, select Benign to limit the logs to non-malicious verdicts.
If you do not specify techniques in this filter, verdicts associated with any possible MITRE ATT&CK technique are displayed.

user-cap.summary: The limits page caps users per NSS feed filter at 1,024, while the SaaS Security article says there is no limit.

quotes: | Number of Users per NSS Feed Filter | 1,024 users |

positions.says: The limits page lists 1,024 users per NSS feed filter (shared.nss.feeds:filter-caps).

quotes: There's no limit to the number of users that you can select.

positions.says: The SaaS Security feed article says there is no limit to the users that can be selected.

user-cap.impact: Whether a SaaS Security feed filter is exempt from the 1,024 cap cannot be settled from the vendor text.

value-logic.title: How filter values and filter fields combine
value-logic.detail: The articles say multiple selections are allowed and give one example of two filters on different fields (filters-and). They never state a general rule for how filters on different fields combine, nor how several values in one field combine, so AND across fields and OR within a field are implied but not stated.

http-web-filter-absences.title: Filters the HTTP web feed does not have
http-web-filter-absences.detail: Diffing the HTTP web article against the TCP one showed no AI/ML Detection Source filter and no Include or Exclude options on its URL Classes, Super Categories and Categories filters, while the Cloud web article has AI/ML Detection Source. An absence cannot be quoted, so it is not claimed.

mcas-who-group.title: Whether the MCAS feed filters by user
mcas-who-group.detail: The MCAS article lists Locations under its Who group, where every other web feed lists Users. That is probably a doc error, but no source says so, and the article does not state that MCAS cannot filter by user.
